_description: Core workflow doctrine for the AI Niagara Artist system. This defines how the agent should bootstrap, author, validate, and iterate on Niagara effects.
bootstrap_sequence: Create a clean empty Niagara System instead of duplicating a full effect by default.
Search for reusable Niagara template systems and pick emitters that match the intended layer role.
Add template emitters into the clean system one layer at a time.
Fallback to empty emitters only when no suitable template emitter exists.
authoring_loop: Inspect the emitter stack and module inputs before applying edits.
Adjust artist-facing controls in a stable order: quantity, lifetime, size, color, opacity, velocity, forces, renderer, material.
Compile and save after each meaningful batch of stack edits.
Review the assembled system and spawn a preview actor for visual verification.
verification_loop: Review stack/module structure for missing required layers or modules.
Compile Niagara deterministically and inspect diagnostics.
Spawn the system in the level and capture screenshots or probes for visual iteration.
guardrails: Do not author complex stacks from zero when a template emitter can provide a stable foundation.
Prefer artist-facing high-level controls before low-level module-input surgery.
Keep emitter roles separate: core body, volume/fill, accents, smoke, sparks, distortion.
Treat renderer/material setup and compile verification as required completion steps, not optional polish.
